Aggregate and cancel equal Cells first, then require at most one positive site in the signed difference. D is the sum of all twenty complete raw three-axis marginal L1 norms.

The sharp 3/20 constant requires N=2P, negative sites on individual axis lines and equal six-axis aggregate negative masses. The signed difference is analytical bookkeeping, not a negative BRC branch. methods.name: local divisor-layer lift and factor-forcing spectrum probe
capabilities: classify target T as factor-forcing whenever tau(n) does not divide T
prove lambda_T(n)=p_min^(r-2) for squarefree n with k primes and T=2^(k-1)r, r odd prime
retain all nearby composite divisor-count layers instead of prematurely collapsing to a mode
measure information loss caused by modal compression
run finite exact small-number diagnostics with explicit large-N non-claim boundaries
methods.core_law: If gcd(a,n)=1 then tau(an)=tau(a)tau(n), so tau(n) not dividing T forces every exact lift multiplier to overlap n. For squarefree n with k distinct prime factors and T=2^(k-1)r with r an odd prime, the divisor-product factorization has exactly k factors and forces exponent pattern (r-1,1,...,1), hence the minimal lift is p_min^(r-2).
methods.hard_boundary: The theorem does not provide lambda_T(n) from N alone and exact tau of arbitrary large neighbors can itself require factorization. This is currently an opportunistic observer/research probe, not a claimed large-integer factoring shortcut. Fixed small-layer frequencies are finite diagnostics and must not be extrapolated to RSA scale.

Deterministic single-path problems reduce to E=1, Delta=0 and should not be artificially reinterpreted as multiplicity problems.

methods.name: Odd-N BRC admissible multiplier scan / strong square-gap cascade

methods.core_law: For odd N, m==2 mod 4 cannot satisfy x^2-y^2=mN. The admissible monotone path therefore has 75 states through m<=100. One-step transitions reuse t0.brc_multiplier_transition; two-step skips use a dyadic sqrt((m+2)/m) predictor and at most three odd-width corrections. A square gap must pass both mod-20160 and mod-46189 tables, whose uniform joint pass fraction is 108/46189.
methods.hard_boundary: Parity pruning, quadratic-residue filtering, Lawrence/Lehman/Hart multiplier-Fermat search, and rational factor-ratio selection are classical prior art. The nu(m)^4/m priority is experimental only and is not a theorem, default proof path, RSA shortcut, or asymptotic improvement. Finite timings and finite hit-rate samples do not imply factorization complexity progress. The BRC-specific proved addition is retained-state m->m+2 transport and its composition with the existing multiplier transition tool.

methods.name: BRC multiplier basin / squarefree phase calculus
capabilities: exact integer-only multiplier-induced BRC point cost state
exact source-basin to target-support multiplicity histogram
full-range square multiplier support law H=min(s,2k+1)
balanced dense square-refinement multiplicities q or q+1
stable non-square Beatty support with exact Pell endpoint correction
exact squarefree-core plus finite square-refinement phase composition
explicit Boolean-support versus remainder/multiplicity observer-loss witness
methods.core_law: For m=s^2, a source square-root basin of size N=2k+1 occupies exactly min(s,N) target roots; when s<=N the support is consecutive and multiplicities are the balanced q/q+1 partition. For fixed non-square m in the eventual no-skip regime, H_m(k)=Delta_m(k)+1-1[D_m(k+1)<m], where Delta is a two-valued Beatty increment and the exceptional D<m set is generalized-Pell and zero-density. For m=a^2 d, retaining the d-stage root/remainder (y,rho) gives exact final root ay+u and remainder a^2 rho-2ayu-u^2 with 0<=u<a.
methods.hard_boundary: Finite/exact integer BRC calculus only. The Pell count uses classical Pell-unit theory; no factorization speedup, asymptotic complexity improvement, Foundation promotion, signed cancellation semantics, or recovery of erased remainder/provenance is claimed. The non-square closed support formula requires the declared sufficient no-skip regime m<=4k^2; outside it use multiplier_basin_profile rather than extrapolating the formula.

methods.name: BRC consecutive-multiplier root/remainder transition
capabilities: exact fixed-N multiplier root/remainder sequence through m=100 with only one initial N-dependent root materialization
checked-in 99-entry dyadic gamma predictor table for N up to 4096 bits
exact precision specialization by right shift from one high-precision table
cached exact predictor fallback above the static cap
proved at-most-two local BRC odd-width correction steps per transition
exact ceiling completion gap directly from retained root/remainder
composition with classical square-residue prefilter without semantic conflation
methods.core_law: With gamma_m=sqrt((m+1)/m)-1, choose B so J_m<2^(B-1), C_m=floor(2^B gamma_m), d0=floor(C_m J_m/2^B). Then J_(m+1)-(J_m+d0) is in {0,1,2}. The provisional remainder is R_m+N-d0(2J_m+d0); subtracting successive odd basin widths at most twice yields exactly R_(m+1).
methods.hard_boundary: Finite exact integer multiplier scan only; checked-in static performance fast path N<=4096 bits and m<=100. Larger-N predictor generation is cached but no one-off speed claim is made. Performance evidence is environment-specific constant-factor timing. No asymptotic factorization speedup, no novelty claim for multiplier-Fermat/Lehman square-gap factoring, no recovery after erasing R_m, and no Foundation promotion.

methods.name: BRC stride-8 quotient/remainder jet tail
capabilities: decompose the odd-N mod-8 sparse multiplier stream into five fixed-step residue orbits
seed every orbit with three exact Euclidean quotient samples, exactly fifteen divisions total
quadratically extrapolate the next quotient and recover the exact quotient/remainder by at most four signed denominator repairs
prove the quotient third-difference correction interval [-4,4] under the common linear tail and m>=962h
retain exact quotient remainder and bounded first/second finite-difference repair coordinates
avoid a fresh large-integer quotient division and generic quotient-times-denominator product after seeding
compose with the order-one linear BRC root closure and the staged square-gap residue cascade
provide an allocation-free in-place scan path for large-integer hot loops
operate without a multiplier-horizon table or upper multiplier bound
methods.core_law: For one fixed source residue class modulo 8, let q_m=floor(2hJ_m/(4m+h)) and rho_m be the exact Euclidean remainder. Consecutive visits differ by 8. Under 4m^5>=N and m>=962h, the smooth third-difference plus source-root phase has magnitude below one, while the floor phase contributes strictly between -4 and 4; hence epsilon=q_(m+8)-3q_m+3q_(m-8)-q_(m-16) lies in [-4,4]. Carrying rho and P=(Delta q+Delta^2 q)(D+32) yields the exact provisional residual S=rho+2h(J'-J)-32q-P, normalized by at most four additions/subtractions of D'=D+32. Five orbits times three samples require fifteen seed divisions; all later quotient states are exact recurrence states.
methods.hard_boundary: This extends t0.brc_linear_deep_tail and composes with t0.brc_square_gap_cascade; it is not a new top-level tool family. The proof controls exact multiplier-state transport only and does not shorten a Lehman/Hart-style search horizon or establish a factorization-complexity improvement. Finite Python benchmarks favor the jet only for sufficiently large integers (around 4096 bits in the committed environment); small-size routing should retain native division. The exact quotient remainder must not be collapsed to quotient-only or a fitted real trend.
